title: Y. Steinsapir
summary: A journalist who created an independent weekly newspaper.
uncertaintyNote: The given-name initial and OCR around the name are unclear.

enrichment.markdown:
- **Y. G. Steinsapir (Shteynsapir / שטײנסאַפּיר).** The outside record that most directly expands this identification is a JewishGen-hosted chapter on Białystok’s prewar Jewish press. It describes Steinsapir as a witty writer who founded an independent weekly and used it to publish feuilletons; it also lists his weekly among the city’s Jewish papers. This supports the memorial book’s account of him as a journalist, but supplies no full biography, dates, family, or wartime fate. [JewishGen, “The Jewish Press before the Holocaust”](https://www.jewishgen.org/Yizkor/Bialystok1/biay089.html)

- **S. Lampert, Koritsin (Korycin), and Białystok.** The same chapter identifies Sh. Lampert as a writer and sculptor living in Korycin, a small town near Białystok. It says he worked for years on a trilogy, published in book form, with chapters also appearing in Białystok’s daily paper. This establishes a literary connection and links Korycin to the city’s press network, but does not establish a personal or family relationship with Steinsapir. [JewishGen, “The Jewish Press before the Holocaust”](https://www.jewishgen.org/Yizkor/Bialystok1/biay089.html)

- **Isaac Vysatsky and Aharon Brezinsky.** The chapter names these writers as contributors to Pesach Kaplan’s *Unzer Leben* and says both also published in the *Forverts*. It gives Vysatsky’s subject as love-themed novellas and characterizes Brezinsky’s work as restoring figures and scenes from the lost Lithuanian-Polish shtetl. The source does not provide dates or family details here. [JewishGen, “The Jewish Press before the Holocaust”](https://www.jewishgen.org/Yizkor/Bialystok1/biay089.html)

- **Pesach Kaplan and *Our Life*.** The paper began as *Dos Naye Lebn* in 1919, edited by Kaplan, and took the name *Unzer Lebn* in 1931. A separate account describes Kaplan as editor-in-chief and the paper as a major outlet for Białystok’s writers. The memorial history also remembers Kaplan as a publicist and writer; it recounts that he dedicated a song to Jewish men seized and murdered after the German occupation. These sources add the newspaper’s chronology and Kaplan’s importance, but do not establish the fate of every contributor. [JewishGen, press history and city chronology](https://www.jewishgen.org/Yizkor/Bialystok1/biay089.html) · [JewishGen, Kaplan memorial passage](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/Bialystok1/biay243.html)

- **Chanawitch, Yosef Rubinlicht, and *Warsaw Express*.** The press chapter identifies Osher Tshonovitsh (a spelling variant of Chanawitch) as a reporter associated with the *Warsaw Ekspres* collective, and Yosef Rubinlikht as a reporter noted for popular humor. It gives no further biographical or family information for either man. [JewishGen, “The Jewish Press before the Holocaust”](https://www.jewishgen.org/Yizkor/Bialystok1/biay089.html)

- **Limits of the outside findings.** A separate JewishGen index lists a **Yisrael-Gedaliah Steinsapir** in another Białystok chronicle, but the index alone does not show that he is Y. G. Steinsapir, the journalist; the name match is suggestive, not proof. [JewishGen, *Pinkos Bialystok* index](https://kehilalinks.jewishgen.org/bialygen/Pinkos1_Index.htm) I found no securely attributable family relationships, dates, migration, deportation record, or fate for the journalist or the named associates in the sources located.

sources.title: JewishGen, “The Jewish Press before the Holocaust”
